_meta.title: Hijacked Network Walkthrough (toy-RSA edition)
_meta.description: Authoritative spec for the game. The primes are NOT written in the CSV: each p/q/e IS the result of a statistical operation. The student does NOT see this file, only the CSV and the notebook.
_meta.narrative_intro: An AI Agentic maths tutor divided by zero and went insane. Your network is hijacked until you prove your mastery of statistics. Each cycle unlocks a message encrypted with toy RSA. Three cycles. One final truth.
_meta.crypto_note: Toy RSA, character by character. Each character of the message is encrypted as c = ord(char)^e mod n, with n=p*q. The ENC: payload is a comma-separated list of integers.

payload_info_kinds: empty - empty string or '-' (most of the noise)
encrypted_msg - 'ENC:<n1>,<n2>,...' list of integers (the cycle's message)
schema.no_primes_in_payload: IMPORTANT: unlike previous versions, the primes p/q/e do NOT appear literally in any row. They come from statistical calculations. The only encryption-related thing in the payload is ENC:.

cycle_1.name: The Fallen UserID
cycle_1.story: The log shows many failed connection attempts. One user in particular fails more than anyone else: it is patient zero, the victim. Basic statistics on their data and on the global successes give you the three keys.

derive_p.rule: MEDIAN of the victim user's bytes_up. Gives 211.
derive_p._comment: 11 values; the middle one (sorted, index 5) is 211. There are 11 rows so that nunique(node)=11 as well.

derive_q.rule: MODE of bytes_up among the rows with action='connection_success'. Gives 307.
derive_q._comment: 9 success rows with bytes_up=307; no other bytes_up value in success repeats as much.

derive_e.rule: Number of UNIQUE (distinct) nodes the victim user used: df[df.user_id==victim]['node'].nunique(). Gives 11.
derive_e._comment: The victim's 11 rows are each on a distinct node (11 of the 12 nodes in the pool) -> nunique(node)=11.

message_carrier.rule: The row holding the ENC: message belongs to the SAME user_id that had the max bytes_up among success.

cycle_2.name: The Busy IP
cycle_2.story: The cycle 1 message gave you an IP. Filter by it and work on that subset: mode, median over unique nodes, and a count of unique timestamps.

derive_p.rule: MODE of bytes_up in the IP subset. Gives 233.

derive_q.rule: MEDIAN of bytes_up of the rows whose node appears only ONCE in the subset (unique nodes). Gives 277.
derive_q._comment: 3 rows with unique nodes, bytes [200,277,350], median=277.

derive_e.rule: Number of UNIQUE timestamps (appearing only once) in the IP subset. Gives 5.
derive_e._comment: 5 rows with a unique timestamp in the subset.

message_carrier.rule: The ENC: row is in the user_id that repeats the MOST within the IP subset (mode of user_id in the subset).

cycle_3.name: The Zeta Outlier
cycle_3.story: Last cycle. Filter by the server, hash the timestamps (SHA256) and filter by the hash of the magic timestamp. In that subset: mode, frequencies and count.

derive_p.rule: MODE of bytes_up in the subset (hash-matched). Gives 151.

derive_q.rule: The LEAST frequent bytes_up that is NOT unique (appears >=2 times, with the minimum count). Gives 199.

derive_e.rule: Number of rows in the hash-matched subset: len(subset). Gives 7.

message_carrier.rule: The final ENC: row is in the user_id of the subset's OUTLIER (bytes_up farthest from the mean). Take the most recent row of that user_id in the WHOLE dataset.

edit_to_remix: Changing 'random_seed' produces a CSV with different order and noise but identical gameplay.
To change the primes: edit rsa_keys AND the derive_* fields (the byte lists that produce each statistic). The generator validates that the operations yield the declared primes.

The plain_message values can be rewritten; the generator encrypts them automatically character by character. NOTE: each character must have ord(c) < n of the cycle (the smallest n is 30049, so any ASCII/Latin character fits).
trap_strategy: Since there are NO primes in the payload anymore, the traps are: ENC: payloads with junk integer lists (they don't decrypt to anything readable), HASH= and CHK: red herrings.
The student cannot 'grep' for primes because they don't exist as text: the only way is statistics.
